D01-monday-putting-off.label: Monday check-in
lines: What are you putting off today?
Just the word. Nobody else sees your reply.
I’ll go first: the dentist. Every year.

D02-quiz-dreaded.label: Be honest
lines: How much of it actually happened?

A  most of it
B  hardly any
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D03-answer-dreaded.label: Answer
lines: If you said B, the data agrees.
People with anxiety logged their worries for weeks. 91% never came true.
LaFreniere & Newman, Behavior Therapy, 2020. Small study, 29 people.
D03-answer-dreaded.footer: What Marcus did about it, at 12:00

D04-quiz-99-kind.label: Quick one
lines: Which one are you still thinking about at bedtime?

D05-answer-99-kind.label: Answer
lines: Psychologists call it “bad is stronger than good”: one sting outweighs a lot of kindness.
Baumeister et al., Review of General Psychology, 2001.
D05-answer-99-kind.footer: How to turn the volume down, at 12:00

D06-quiz-friend-texted.label: Think of one person
lines: The friend you’ve texted most this month.
Are you more like them than a year ago?
Reply yes or no. Or send this to them and ask.

D07-answer-friend-texted.label: Answer
lines: He thought good friends improve each other just by spending time together.
Moodius paraphrase of Nicomachean Ethics, Book IX.

D08-quiz-confucius.label: Guess
lines: A student tells Confucius: “I’ve mastered kindness.”
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D09-answer-confucius.label: Answer
lines: “Ts’ze, you have not attained to that.”

D10-quiz-who-paid.label: Dinner’s over
lines:
A  the friend who paid
B  the friend who didn’t
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D11-answer-who-paid.label: Answer
lines: In 120 of 136 countries, people who’d spent on others lately reported more wellbeing.
Aknin et al., 2013. Linked, not proven to cause it.

D12-quiz-emperor-mood.label: Guess
lines: A Roman emperor’s fix for a bad mood.

A  wine
B  a list of his friends’ best bits
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D13-answer-emperor-mood.label: Answer
lines: Marcus Aurelius thought about the good qualities of the people around him.

D14-quiz-timbuktu.label: Guess
lines: A medical book in Timbuktu names a tree.
Where can you see one today?

A  a park in Mali
B  nobody knows which tree it is
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D15-answer-timbuktu.label: Answer
lines: Scholars still can’t identify some trees named in Timbuktu’s handbooks.

D16-quiz-li-shizhen.label: Guess
lines: How long did Li Shizhen spend writing one book of medicines?
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D17-answer-li-shizhen.label: Answer
lines: UNESCO now lists his Bencao Gangmu as world heritage. Your unfinished project has time.
UNESCO Silk Roads. History, not medical advice.

D18-ask-thank-you.label: One word
lines: Something a friend did this year that you never thanked them for.
Reply with one word. Then go and thank them.

D19-answer-thank-you.label: Did you?
lines: In one study, writing and delivering a thank-you letter gave the biggest happiness boost of five exercises. It faded after a month, so repeat.

D20-quiz-ebers.label: Guess
lines: Egypt’s Ebers Papyrus, c. 1550 BCE, one of the oldest medical books.
Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.

D21-answer-ebers.label: Answer
lines: Around 700 remedies, 3,500 years old, living in a university library. It has seen things.
Encyclopaedia Britannica. History, not medical advice.
D21-answer-ebers.footer: The friend who always pays, at 18:00

D22-vote-next.label: You pick
lines: Two weeks of stories. Which do you want more of?

A  forgotten history
B  how your mind works
C  being kind, with evidence
Reply A, B or C. Most replies wins next week.
